text:
emily: FYI escalation from customer (Jensen). They have latency spikes because their traffic is being routed to us-west even though they send X-Redwood-Region: eu-west. Seeing 200–300ms extra and occasional 502 when eu cluster is full. Repro attached.

raj: Can you paste a minimal repro curl and the response headers?

emily: Curl they used:
```
curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -H 'X-Redwood-Region: eu-west' \
  https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/generate
```
Response shows: 
```
> HTTP/1.1 200 OK
> x-upstream-region: us-west
> x-redwood-fallback: true
```
Also sometimes 502 with x-upstream-region: us-west even immediately after request with eu header.

liam: Quick thought — Gateway (envoy) has an L7 route that rewrites/passes headers. Maybe header match precedence isn't honoring the explicit X-Redwood-Region and falls back to route-level region affinity. Which gateway build are you hitting?

emily: gateway-prod v1.26.3 (envoy build), route config attached from ops: 
```yaml
- match: { prefix: "/v1/" }
  route: { cluster: api-cluster, headers_to_add: [{ header: { key: "x-upstream-region", value: "us-west" } }] }
```
Not sure why header match isn't overriding.

liam: That headers_to_add will always inject us-west at route time unless header rewrite rules include substitution based on incoming header. Envoy header transform precedence can be tricky — if a route always adds x-upstream-region it can overwrite client header. Need to check remove/append semantics.

raj: Can you show the raw request received by the gateway (from customer) — specifically if the incoming X-Redwood-Region header arrives intact? If it's being dropped earlier (LB or CDN) that's a different issue.

emily: Verified with tcpdump on edge: incoming request includes X-Redwood-Region: eu-west. But the route config in gateway injects x-upstream-region: us-west unconditionally. So the gateway is not honoring incoming header as intended.

ops-oncall: Immediate mitigation: roll a quick route update to stop adding x-upstream-region unconditionally. Change headers_to_add -> append_action: ADD_IF_ABSENT or use header_value_match to prefer incoming header. I'll push a patch to canary.

deploy-bot: canary deploy started for gateway-prod routes (canary id: canary-20260317-01)

liam: Follow-up — this looks like an Envoy L7 behavior change between builds where headers_to_add semantics changed. If we rely on add overwriting, we should be explicit. Create an issue to pin behavior and upgrade to envoy 1.27.x where bugfixes for header append semantics landed.

emily: Applied canary change: removed unconditional headers_to_add and added: 
```yaml
headers_to_add:
  - header: { key: "x-upstream-region", value: "%REQ(X-REDWOOD-REGION)%" }
    append_action: APPEND_IF_EXISTS
```
Canary shows eu-west preserved for customer traffic. :thumbsup:

ops-oncall: Rolling to 30% then 100% after monitoring for 10m. Also open a postmortem with the customer and suggest token-scoped regional pinning as long-term.

emily: Opening internal ticket and including envoy upgrade plan. Will notify customer with timeline. Thanks all.
